summary: Conecuh County, Alabama, tower: a 1962 Aermotor MC-39 replacement for an original wooden tower, run by the Alabama Forestry Commission; NHLR-registered 2011.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-39 tower with 7x7-foot cab, replacing an original 100-foot wooden tower

events.note: The Alabama Forestry Commission replaced the original 100-foot wooden tower with an Aermotor MC-39 tower with a 7x7-foot cab
Registered January 3, 2011; nominated by Thomas Kaufmann

evidence.supports: tower is in Conecuh County, Alabama
administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
original tower was a 100-foot wooden tower
evidence.quote: The original Brooks Fire Tower was a 100' wooden tower.

evidence.supports: AFC replaced it in 1962 with an Aermotor MC-39 with a 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: In 1962 the Alabama Forestry Commission replaced it with this 100; Aermotor MC-39 tower with 7'x7' cab.

corrections.why: No fetched source states the tower's current condition. The Register page lists the tower and includes a drone video, but no text says it stands today.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 375 ft (114 m); TopoQuest gives 380 ft MSL. The story reports both; the difference is not explained.
The Register's sentence on the 1962 tower prints its height as a garbled '100;'. No height is recorded for the replacement tower.

notes_for_editor: NHLR is the only tower-specific history. TopoQuest confirms the name, county and approximate location (its coordinates agree with the Register's to about 0.001 degree) but nothing about the history. The brief's 1962 build year matches the Register's replacement date; the event is recorded as replaced because the Register describes a replacement. Forest Lookouts' cached brooks.html page covers a Pennsylvania site, so it was not used. Two WebSearch queries found no build history. The brief's status standing is not stated by any fetched source, hence the proposed correction. No photos added: the Register's photos are not listed with URLs or licenses in the page text I read.
